review: 112.3-1: Painter's Servant makes itself red, so Blue Elemental Blast's destroy mode targets it and the base's castability verdict did not hinge on the spell's color; the decision and expected now name the counter mode's legal targets.

scenarios.title: A cast card is a spell on the stack, so spell-targeting effects can target it, and a card in hand or on the battlefield is not
decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping both Forests.
A passes priority; B receives priority with Grizzly Bears on the stack and is asked whether Essence Scatter can be cast (it is not cast in this scenario).

variants.label: on-the-stack
variants.expected: While Grizzly Bears is on the stack it is a creature spell: Essence Scatter is castable by B with Grizzly Bears as its legal target.

variants.label: already-resolved
variants.delta: B passes priority with Grizzly Bears on the stack, so it resolves; B is then asked about Essence Scatter in the beginning of combat step.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a permanent on the battlefield, no longer a spell: Essence Scatter has no legal target and cannot be cast.

variants.label: not-cast
variants.delta: A does not cast Grizzly Bears; it stays in A's hand and A passes priority with an empty stack to the beginning of combat step, where B is asked about Essence Scatter.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a card in hand, not a spell: Essence Scatter has no legal target and cannot be cast.

scenarios.title: A spell stays on the stack until it resolves or is countered
decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping both Forests.
B casts Essence Scatter targeting the Grizzly Bears spell, tapping both Islands.
Both players pass; Essence Scatter resolves.

variants.label: countered
variants.expected: Essence Scatter resolves and counters the Grizzly Bears spell: Grizzly Bears moves from the stack to A's graveyard and never reaches the battlefield. Essence Scatter moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: unrelated-response
variants.delta: B casts Shock targeting A's face, tapping the Mountain, instead of casting Essence Scatter.
variants.expected: Shock resolves first and A is at 18 life. Grizzly Bears stays on the stack through that resolution, then resolves and enters the battlefield under A's control. It is not countered.

variants.label: no-response
variants.delta: B casts nothing and passes priority.
variants.expected: The Grizzly Bears spell resolves and enters the battlefield under A's control; A's and B's graveyards are empty.

scenarios.title: A copy of a spell is itself a spell and can be countered as one
decisions: A casts Shock targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Mountain, and keeps priority.
A casts Twincast targeting the Shock spell, tapping both Islands.
Both players pass; Twincast resolves and creates a copy of Shock; A keeps the target Grizzly Bears for the copy.
A passes priority with the Shock copy on top of the stack.
B casts Negate targeting the Shock copy, tapping both Islands.
Both players pass; Negate resolves.

variants.label: copy-negated
variants.expected: Negate legally targets the Shock copy and counters it: the copy leaves the stack and ceases to exist, it is not put into any graveyard. The original Shock then resolves and Grizzly Bears (2/2) takes 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard. Negate is in B's graveyard; Twincast and Shock are in A's graveyard.

variants.label: no-negate
variants.delta: B does not cast Negate and passes priority.
variants.expected: The Shock copy resolves and deals 2 damage to Grizzly Bears, which moves to B's graveyard in the state-based check. The original Shock then resolves with Grizzly Bears already gone, so it fizzles. Twincast and the original Shock are in A's graveyard, and the copy ceases to exist.

scenarios.forge_notes: Twincast's copy is created on the stack by CopySpellAbility; Negate's ValidTgts is Card.nonCreature, so the copy must count as a noncreature spell on the stack.

scenarios.title: A copy of a card that a player casts is a spell

setup.notes: Isochron Scepter has A's exiled Shock imprinted on it (exiled with it).

decisions: A activates Isochron Scepter ({2}, {T}), tapping both Mountains.
Both players pass; the ability resolves: A copies the imprinted Shock and casts the copy without paying its mana cost, targeting Grizzly Bears.
A passes priority with the Shock copy on the stack.
B casts Negate targeting the Shock copy, tapping both Islands.
Both players pass; Negate resolves.

variants.label: copy-negated
variants.expected: The cast copy is a spell, so Negate legally targets it and counters it. The copy ceases to exist and is not put into a graveyard. Grizzly Bears is undamaged and stays on the battlefield. The original Shock card remains in exile with Isochron Scepter.

variants.label: no-response
variants.delta: B does not cast Negate and passes priority.
variants.expected: The Shock copy resolves and deals 2 damage to Grizzly Bears, which moves to B's graveyard in the state-based check. The copy ceases to exist and the original Shock card remains in exile.

variants.label: copy-declined
variants.delta: When the Scepter ability resolves, A chooses not to copy the card, so no copy is cast.
variants.expected: No spell is put on the stack; Negate has no legal target and cannot be cast. Grizzly Bears is undamaged and the Shock card remains in exile.

scenarios.forge_notes: The Scepter's imprint is normally set by its enters trigger; the setup needs the exiled card remembered as imprinted and exiled with the Scepter.

scenarios.title: A spell's controller is the player who put it on the stack, including a copy of an opponent's spell
decisions: B casts Divination, tapping all three Islands.
B passes priority; A casts Twincast targeting the Divination spell, tapping both Islands.
Both players pass; Twincast resolves and creates a copy of Divination controlled by A.
Both players pass; the copy resolves, then both players pass and the original Divination resolves.

variants.label: copied
variants.expected: The copy is controlled by A, so A draws two cards (hand: Mountain, Mountain). The original is controlled by B, so B draws two cards (hand: Forest, Forest). The copy ceases to exist; B's Divination moves to B's graveyard and Twincast to A's graveyard.

variants.label: no-copy
variants.delta: A does not cast Twincast and passes priority.
variants.expected: Only the original Divination resolves: B draws two cards and A draws none. A's hand still holds Twincast and B's Divination moves to B's graveyard.

scenarios.title: A copy of an opponent's card that a player is instructed to create and cast belongs to that player

setup.notes: Libraries are listed top first. Divination is owned by B and sits in B's graveyard.

decisions: A casts Spelltwine targeting Shock in A's graveyard and Divination in B's graveyard, tapping all six Islands.
Both players pass; Spelltwine resolves: both cards are exiled and A creates a copy of each.
A casts the copy of Shock without paying its mana cost, targeting B's face.
A casts the copy of Divination without paying its mana cost.
Both players pass; the Divination copy resolves, then both players pass and the Shock copy resolves.

variants.label: copy-of-divination
variants.expected: A is the owner and controller of the Divination copy, so A draws two cards (hand: Forest, Forest) and B draws none. B is at 18 life. Both original cards are in exile and Spelltwine is exiled; neither graveyard gains a card, since the copies cease to exist.

variants.label: copy-of-shock
variants.delta: The card in B's graveyard is Shock instead of Divination.
variants.expected: A casts two copies of Shock, both owned and controlled by A, each targeting B's face. B is at 16 life and A draws no cards. Both original Shock cards and Spelltwine are exiled.

variants.label: no-opposing-card
variants.expected: Spelltwine cannot be cast: it has no legal target in an opponent's graveyard, so no copy is ever created and nothing changes.

scenarios.forge_notes: Spelltwine plays its copies through Play with CopyCard and WithoutManaCost; the second target is Instant.OppOwn or Sorcery.OppOwn.

scenarios.title: A spell's characteristics are its printed ones as modified by continuous effects

setup.notes: Painter's Servant entered with red chosen as its color. Grizzly Bears is a green creature.

decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping both Forests.

A passes priority; B receives priority with the Grizzly Bears spell on the stack and is asked whether Blue Elemental Blast can be cast with its counter-target-red-spell mode; it is not cast in this scenario.

variants.label: servant-red
variants.expected: The Grizzly Bears spell is green and red. Blue Elemental Blast's counter mode has the Grizzly Bears spell as a legal target. (Its destroy mode also has Painter's Servant, now a red permanent, as a legal target.)

variants.label: no-servant
variants.delta: Painter's Servant is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: The Grizzly Bears spell is only green. Blue Elemental Blast's counter mode has no legal target, its destroy mode has none either, and it cannot be cast.

scenarios.forge_notes: Painter's Servant's AddColor applies to AffectedZone All, which must include the stack; its color is chosen as it enters, so the setup must preset ChosenColor to red.

scenarios.title: A characteristic change applied to a permanent spell persists on the permanent
decisions: A casts Black Knight, tapping both Swamps.
B casts Sleight of Mind targeting the Black Knight spell, tapping Island, and changes the color word white to red.
Both players pass; Sleight of Mind resolves, then both players pass and the Black Knight spell resolves.
Both players pass with an empty stack until the beginning of combat step; B is asked whether Shock can be cast targeting Black Knight (the cast is not made in this scenario).

variants.label: text-changed
variants.expected: The text change made to the spell continues to apply to the permanent: Black Knight on the battlefield has protection from red, so Shock cannot legally target it and is not castable at it.

variants.label: no-change
variants.delta: B does not cast Sleight of Mind.
variants.expected: Black Knight keeps its printed protection from white, so the red Shock can legally target it and is castable at it.

scenarios.forge_notes: Needs Forge's ChangeText with Duration Permanent on a spell on the stack to carry over to the permanent, including the keyword's color word.
